title: Color picker misbehavior while using Windows Color Filter Accessibility feature.
author: AVMiraga
summary: With a Windows accessibility color filter enabled, Color Picker reports the post-filter displayed pixel rather than the source application's original color, including transform rounding differences.
next_action: Close as expected screen-sampling behavior and document that accessibility filters affect sampled display colors.

confidence.rationale: The capture semantics and the limitation of a one-sample inverse are clear from the discussion.

judgment.rationale: A maintainer explains that Color Picker samples the actual displayed pixel; reversing an accessibility transform is not a constant per-channel subtraction and would not reliably recover source color.
evidence: The report changes only Windows 11 Deuteranopia Color Filter and observes shifted sampled values.
A maintainer states the picker captures the actual pixel value and filter rounding introduces error.
The suggested fixed red-channel subtraction is based on one sample and cannot represent a general color transform.
judgment.recommended_action: Close as expected screen-sampling behavior and document that accessibility filters affect sampled display colors.

fix_assessment.rationale: Sampling the post-composition displayed pixel is expected behavior; the proposed inverse adjustment is not generally valid.

issue_context.summary: With a Windows accessibility color filter enabled, Color Picker reports the post-filter displayed pixel rather than the source application's original color, including transform rounding differences.
known_information: The behavior was reported on PowerToys 0.70.0 and 0.73.0.
The filter is applied by Windows, outside the source application.
The screenshot demonstrates a changed displayed color under Deuteranopia filtering.
inferences: Recovering the pre-filter source value would require reliable access to the original composition content or an invertible transform, neither established here.
issue_context.analysis: Color Picker's observable input is the composed screen. Documentation can set expectations without introducing a fragile filter-specific inverse.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and both comments.
Evaluated the proposed constant subtraction against the maintainer's transform/rounding explanation.

actions.label: Document color-filter sampling behavior

comment.body: Color Picker samples the pixel after Windows has applied the accessibility color filter, so the returned value represents the displayed color rather than the source application's original value. A fixed per-channel subtraction cannot safely undo a color transform and its rounding. Please close this as expected screen-sampling behavior and document that enabled Windows color filters affect picked values.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
